title: The focus check stops crying theft about one walk's own declared drags
goal: After most tasks the loop checks that walks leave the person's keyboard and focus alone. About one check in three it prints a red alarm, A WALK TOOK THE PERSON'S FOCUS, about the same walk, which drags clips and is allowed to take the front for those drags. The other checks call the identical run fine. Either the alarm is wrong and should stop, or the walk really grabs the front a step early and that should stop; someone reading the loop must be able to trust the alarm.
notes: Evidence, queue/loop.log and queue/loop.log.1: across the last 16 rotating checks this walk read 'as declared' 11 times and 'TOOK FOCUS' 5 times (2026-10-10 01:14, 07:37, 10:04 local; 2026-10-10 23:41; 2026-10-11 05:37), always with the same 20 ticks lost. The alarm lines blame step 9 (snapshot) or step 10 (expectClip), and step 25 (snapshot), each 'activated com.dzearing.photonz.probe'; the declared drag steps are 11, 20, 26 and 38 (windowDrag). A non-drag step activating is what turns 'as declared' into 'TOOK FOCUS' (queue/bin/focus-drill.sh around line 180, the 'declared' set and stepAt, which places a moment by the walk's log time plus a zero worked out from done.json's mtime). Theory, not checked: the activation that belongs to the drag at step 11 or 26 lands a moment early on the clock and is put on the step before. The alarm says 'this is a bug in the walk harness or the app, not in the walk'. Filed by the 2026-10-11 digest.
acceptance: Reproduce first: run queue/bin/focus-drill.sh a-clip-s-sound-is-linked-under-it-walk ten times (with nobody at the Mac, since the walk drags) and record how many read 'as declared' and how many 'TOOK FOCUS', and which steps each blames

Say in this task's log which it is: the probe really activating during a step that is not a drag, or the check placing a drag's own activation on the step before it (for example the step clock being a few milliseconds off)
After the fix, ten runs in a row read 'as declared' or 'clean', and the drill still reads TOOK FOCUS for a walk that really takes the front outside a declared drag (show one)
The standing focus check after a rotating check prints no red alarm for this walk across a day of the loop's checks (count it from queue/loop.log)

log.note: Count corrected: 17 rotating checks in the two logs ran this walk; 12 read 'as declared' and 5 'TOOK FOCUS'.

2026-10-12 digest: a related trend, logged here because it did not earn its own task. 65 of 887 walks now declare front: true (27 on 2026-09-26). Seven touched in the last day: camera-keys-row-walk, camera-settings-on-the-frame-walk, f-puts-a-video-full-screen-walk, key-a-title-s-scale-walk, properties-pane-walk, properties-reset-walk, the-menu-bar-stays-still-while-playing-walk. The usual reason given is a SwiftUI tap that answers only in the active app. Each one is skipped by rotating checks while someone is at the Mac and is checked only by the daily full set. If the count keeps climbing, reaching controls through the app's own register instead of a tap is the lever.

Reproduced 2026-10-14 with nobody at the Mac: 10 drill runs, 7 'as declared', 3 'TOOK FOCUS' (run 1 blamed step 37 snapshot; run 2 step 10 expectClip + step 25 snapshot; run 6 step 9 snapshot + step 25 snapshot). Every run lost the same 20 ticks, all inside the four drags.

Which it is: the check, not the walk. Measured each probe activation against the step boundaries: in all 40 drags of the 10 runs the activation came 0 to 27 ms after the step before the drag logged, i.e. at the drag's start (takeTheFrontForADrag). The drill rebuilt the walk's start as done.json mtime minus 'seconds', and 'seconds' is rounded to 10 ms, so a few ms of error put the drag's own activation before the boundary, on the previous step (or two back when an instant expectClip sat between). On the exact clock (new startedAtMS) the same activations land 8 to 22 ms after the boundary.

Fix: the harness writes startedAtMS into done.json (PlaytestHarness.finish); the drill's reader moved out of focus-drill.sh into queue/bin/focus-drill-read.mjs, uses the exact start (mtime fallback for older probes) and gives an event up to 50 ms ahead of a DECLARED drag's start to that drag, nothing else. queue/bin/focus-drill-read-drill.mjs replays the failing run 2 (fixture queue/bin/fixtures/focus-trace-linked-sound.json) and made-up cases: all 13 ok.

After the fix: the 10 saved runs replayed through the new reader all read 'as declared'; 10 fresh drill runs on a probe built with the exact clock all read 'as declared'; a real theft (open -b on the probe while the walk sat in step 2's wait) read TOOK FOCUS blaming step 2 (wait), 3 and 4, with the drags still on their own steps. --check: all 8 standing walks clean or as declared. Scripts/test.sh green (13181 tests). Acceptance 4 (a day of the loop's checks with no red alarm for this walk) can only be counted after a day: grep -A1 'a-clip-s-sound-is-linked-under-it-walk  ' queue/loop.log | grep -c 'TOOK FOCUS' on entries after this commit.
